cards.text: Jesus just told the crowd about a rich man who planned bigger barns for all his grain, until God told him his life would be required of him that very night (Luke 12:16-20). Now Jesus turns to His disciples and says, “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.” What to eat, what to wear: friend, that's the exact list that runs through everybody's head at 2 a.m.

cards.question: Jesus gives the disciples His first reason not to worry. What is it?

cards.text: Then Jesus says to consider the ravens: they don't sow or reap, and they have no storehouse or barn. Not one barn, friend, and that rich man was busy planning BIGGER ones.

cards.question: Jesus says the ravens go hungry because they have no storehouse or barn.
God feeds the ravens, and Jesus says the disciples are much more ___ than the birds.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks, “Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?” I worried in the back of a junk drawer for YEARS, friend, and all it ever added was dust.

cards.question: Jesus calls adding a single hour to your life by worrying a small thing.
Nobody can add even one hour to his life by worrying. So what does Jesus ask the disciples?

answers.text: Why work so hard for more
Why ask God for more time

cards.text: Now Jesus says to consider how the lilies grow: they don't labor or spin. No job, no boss, no clocking in, and they STILL look better than me in this hat.

cards.question: Jesus says not even King ___ in all his glory was adorned like one of these lilies.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, “If that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace…” Here today, furnace tomorrow, friend: that's every batch I ever forgot the timer on.

cards.question: If God clothes grass that is gone by tomorrow, what does Jesus say God will do for the disciples?
Right after saying God will clothe the disciples, Jesus praises them for their great faith.

cards.text: Jesus comes back around: don't be concerned about what you'll eat or drink, and don't worry about it. He says it twice, and good thing, because I'm the one who hits snooze TWICE before I get up.

cards.question: Jesus says the Gentiles of the world strive after all these things. What does He say about the disciples' Father?

answers.text: He wants them to strive harder
He will make them wait first

cards.question: Instead of striving after all these things, what does Jesus tell the disciples to seek?
Jesus says that if the disciples seek their Father's kingdom, the things they need will be added unto them.

cards.text: Then Jesus calls the disciples “little flock” and tells them not to be afraid. I've been called a lot of things, friend, but with this mustache, little has NEVER been one of them.

cards.question: Jesus tells His little flock not to be afraid, because their Father is ___ to give them the kingdom.

cards.text: Then Jesus tells them to sell their possessions and give to the poor. Friend, I can't even throw out an old oven mitt without holding a little goodbye ceremony.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples to provide themselves with purses that will not wear out, an inexhaustible treasure. Where is that treasure?
Jesus says a moth can still destroy that treasure in heaven.
Jesus gives one more reason. He says that where your treasure is, something else will be there also. What is it?

cards.text: Hold that thought, friend. Jesus is still talking, and I'm not taking this apron off yet.
